California realtor, 34, busted at LAX on Chinese espionage charges as creepy texts to Beijing handlers revealed: feds

A Chinese foreign agent was arrested at LAX as she tried to depart for China.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

A California realtor has been arrested at LAX after being accused of spying for China.

Wanying Zhang, also known as “Heather,” was busted at the airport Sunday as she tried to board a flight to Shanghai.

The 34-year-old, who lives in Irvine, Orange County, is accused of working with handlers from the People’s Republic of China to surveil the son of Taiwan’s president Ching-Te Lai.

‘We have a problem with Beijing using Chinese-Americans for their own purposes in California,” AG Bill Essayli said. “They are using them for their own foreign affairs because they are playing the long game to get a competitive advantage over us. She wasn’t spying against us, she was allegedly conducting a campaign on behalf of Beijing.”

A criminal complaint released by the FBI Sunday shows texts between her and other alleged agents about tracking Ting-Yu Lai in Seattle, Washington, where he works for electronics giant Philips.

Surveillance camera photographs also allegedly caught Zhang sitting in a car with an accomplice taking pictures of his house and close relatives.

It is the latest Chinese spying scandal to rock California, months after the mayor of Arcadia was snared in a secret propaganda and fake news campaign for the PRC.

And it comes as tensions between China and Taiwan remain high, with US officials fearing Beijing will try to invade the island at some point next year.

Zhang, who worked for a real estate firm along with her husband Edric Ding, allegedly traveled to Seattle in September 2025 to spy on Ting-Yu Lai, an engineer in his 30s who is based in the US.

The text exchanges described in the federal complaint are a key part of the government’s case against Zhang.

According to the FBI affidavit, investigators obtained WeChat communications from Zhang’s iCloud account that they say show her communicating with two people believed to be Chinese government officials and discussing tasks that eventually led to the surveillance of the son of Taiwan’s president.

During a September 2025 exchange, Zhang allegedly told the Chinese government official that she had seen the Taiwanese president’s son. “It’s that young one,” she said. The official then asked whether Zhang was available for an audio call to discuss the matter, but Zhang responded that she was recording video of him.

At the time, Zhang was allegedly at the son’s residence in Seattle.

“According to the affidavit, Zhang traveled to Seattle in 2025 and, at the direction of PRC officials, surveilled a close relative of a Taiwanese government official, sending photos, videos, and license plate information to those officials,” Essayli said. “She coordinated the trip with an associate and used tradecraft to avoid detection. She never notified the Attorney General she was acting for a foreign government, a federal offense.”

Zhang allegedly also took photos of the residence of the son and sent them to the Chinese government officials she was in touch with.

Zhang’s alleged communications with officials date back to Sept. 2022. They include text messages exchanges with an alleged Chinese government official on WeChat regarding children, investments and differences between the U.S. and China among other things.

At that time, Zhang was just asking the alleged official, “Which bureau in the ministry are you in again?” indicating with the use of “bureau” that the person is connected to the Chinese government.
